name: RESCUE BT2
fullName: Tirofiban for Stroke without Large or Medium-Sized Vessel Occlusion
population: n=1177, adults, NIHSS ≥5 with at least one moderately-to-severely weak limb, four entry routes: ≤24 h and ineligible for reperfusion; progression at 24-96 h; early deterioration after thrombolysis; or no improvement 4-24 h after thrombolysis
teachingPoint: IV tirofiban improved 90-day excellent outcome in non-occlusive, often progressive stroke, with inconsistent secondary endpoints.

name: ATTRACTION
fullName: Adjunct Tirofiban Treatment after Successful Endovascular Thrombectomy Recanalisation in Acute Anterior Circulation Ischaemic Stroke
population: n=1380, median 71 y (IQR 62-77); 591 (43%) female, 789 (57%) male, NIHSS 6-30 (protocol inclusion; anterior-circulation LVO), Randomization within 24 h of onset (last known well), after successful reperfusion by thrombectomy
teachingPoint: Reopens the adjunctive-antiplatelet question specifically for the post-reperfusion window, while the numerically higher symptomatic haemorrhage and the near-uniformly Han Chinese cohort mean it is not yet a general recommendation.

name: RESCUE BT
fullName: Effect of Intravenous Tirofiban vs Placebo Before Endovascular Thrombectomy on Functional Outcomes in Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke
population: n=948, mean 67 y; 391 (41.2%) women, NIHSS not restricted by a protocol NIHSS band (proximal intracranial LVO), ≤24 h from time last known well
finding: DID NOT meet superiority — neutral: median (IQR) 90-day mRS 3 (1-4) with tirofiban vs 3 (1-4) with placebo
teachingPoint: Does not support giving intravenous tirofiban before endovascular thrombectomy: 90-day disability was unchanged and symptomatic hemorrhage was numerically higher.

name: MOST
fullName: Multi-arm Optimization of Stroke Thrombolysis: Adjunctive Intravenous Argatroban or Eptifibatide for Ischemic Stroke
population: n=514, adults ≥18 y, NIHSS ≥6 before intravenous thrombolysis, IV thrombolysis within 3 h of onset; study drug started within 75 min of the start of thrombolysis
finding: DID NOT meet superiority for either adjunct — mean (±SD) utility-weighted 90-day mRS 5.2±3.7 with argatroban, 6.3±3.2 with eptifibatide and 6.8±3.0 with placebo; both adjuncts were numerically WORSE than placebo
teachingPoint: Argues against adding intravenous argatroban or eptifibatide to IV thrombolysis in the first hours after treatment: no reduction in disability, and a numerical mortality excess the trial was stopped too early to characterise.

name: STRATEGY
fullName: Tirofiban for Branch Atheromatous Disease-Related Stroke: The STRATEGY Randomized Clinical Trial
population: n=970, 18-80 (median 63), NIHSS ≤10 with LOC 1a ≤1 (median 3), Within 48 h
teachingPoint: No demonstrated reduction in the prespecified deterioration/recurrent-stroke composite in this selected population.

name: ASSET-IT
fullName: Advancing Stroke Safety and Efficacy Through Early Tirofiban Administration After Intravenous Thrombolysis
population: n=832, adults ≥18 y (registry NCT06134622); baseline age distribution not reported in the abstract, NIHSS 4-25 before IV thrombolysis (registry NCT06134622), IV thrombolysis within 4.5 h of onset (last known well); study drug started within 60 min after thrombolysis
teachingPoint: A large phase 3 double-blind trial in which an early 24-h tirofiban infusion after IV thrombolysis increased excellent 90-day outcome in thrombectomy-ineligible noncardioembolic stroke, with a small sICH excess. It is a single Chinese trial that conflicts with MOST, where a GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor (eptifibatide) given in a similar window did not reduce disability, so it does not by itself replace the standard 24-hour post-lysis antithrombotic hold outside a protocol; the 2026 AHA/ASA guideline rates IV tirofiban IIb (B-R).

name: INSTANT
fullName: Intravenous Tirofiban After Tenecteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke
population: n=359, Adults ≥18 y (registry); mean 66 y; 141 (39.3%) female, NIHSS ≥4 before randomization (registry NCT05604638 and published protocol), Randomized, with study drug started, 4-24 h after IV tenecteplase
teachingPoint: In a single Chinese trial, IV tirofiban started 4-24 h after tenecteplase in non-LVO/MeVO, noncardioembolic non-responders increased 90-day mRS 0-1 (63.8% vs 52.2%) with one sICH. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline, which predates INSTANT, rates IV tirofiban in AIS IIb (efficacy not well established).
